description.purpose: When the decider is sure that something on the screen helps with what was just said, something is shown. Every turn with text becomes ONE call to a fast decider (`provider: decisions`) over the topics the installed apps declare -- no trigger words. A sure verdict opens the topic's window with a working hint and, in the same output, asks the app that owns the topic for its data; blocks then appear as their data arrives, each one bound by the topic's manifest and checked against the display catalogue. Unsure, nothing to show, an error or the deadline: the screen stays as it is and the answer stays text. Every turn that asked leaves one journal row (topic, confidence, lead, also, fallback, the three times, model, round) and never the turn's text. Since 1.1.0 ([#963](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/963), [#965](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/965), [#977](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/977), [#966](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/966)) observed tool calls and results are data for the topics `search` and `work`, the member's residents answer built-in topics (`builtin_topics`) through a read stamped with the member's round, a verdict with missing answers still decides over the answers it has and journals `decision_incomplete`, and a set the screen may not see is exactly a set that never came. A caller can rely on what was never promised before, so it is the second digit. Since [#976](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/976) the decider takes the grant way like every other cell that spends a provider key: `decide` carries `credential_grant_id` (shipped empty, which is no grant) and `credential_wait_ms`, and the rim names `./decide` as the connect point of both halves of the credential lane (`credential_request` out, `in_sealed` in). Installed with a grant and an EMPTY `api_key` -- the switch -- the decider asks the member's own `access` for its key and no installation pulls it from `.env`. A lane joined the rim, so it is the second digit. Since 1.2.0 ([#976](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/976), [#982](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/982)) the presenter reads the daily digest and research answers as residents, its decider cell takes a credential grant, and `credential_request` and `in_sealed` join its lanes. A caller can rely on what was never promised before, so it is the second digit. Since 1.2.1 ([#993](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/993)) `./decide` declares the optional hop key `dropped`, the sampling fields a model's `supported_params` left out; nothing else moved. Since 1.2.2 ([#999](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/999)) `./decide` declares the optional hop key `unverified`, the sampling fields sent without a `supported_params` list to check them; nothing else moved. Since 1.2.3 ([#1027](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1027)) a turn with no member of the screen's round in it asks no decider and opens nothing (journal `foreign_round`), and a member's turn on a screen a third party shares opens a window only on `*` data (param `window_requires_star_data`, default on), and the presenter's own topics can carry a threshold of their own (param `builtin_thresholds`, default empty: every topic keeps `threshold`); no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 1.2.4 ([#1027](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1027)) a member's window on a screen a third party shares shows all of the member's data -- gated by the members of the screen's round that are in the turn, another member's rows stay out -- and `window_requires_star_data` ships off (on keeps the `*`-only window); a turn with no member of the screen's round in it still opens nothing. A default moved, no lane, so it is the third digit. Since 1.2.6 ([#1047](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1047)) `stage` orders no `remove` for a `deadline` whose moment has passed -- a one-shot that struck is gone at the timer, even while its strike still waits in the queue -- and the clock's `schedule_not_found` for a remove that met no order is no fault and no longer leaves as `error` `clock_refused`; every other clock refusal still does. A repair, so it is the third digit.
description.use_when: A member with a screen and at least one app that declares `shows` (its topics). Install it beside them; the order of installation does not matter, because every committed mutation asks the apps for their topics again.
description.not_in_scope: It draws no picture of its own: every block is a catalogue component bound from the app's data sets, with no code per topic. It decides no size and no focus (the screen's curator does), sends the decider no data and no memory, and gates every set and row by the screen's round (`screen_audience`, fail-closed). It owns no port and no channel.
examples: "what is the weather like today" -> the decider is sure about `weather`, lead `today`: a window with a working hint, then the hourly list as the data arrives
"thanks, that's all" -> the decider answers `none`: nothing on the screen, one journal row `no_topic`
the lead's data carries only rows of another round: the topic's standard block stands instead, journal `invalid`
